chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who divorces his wife: 'It is for him that he reverts [to her without a new contract].' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot give the final divorce until he touches her [consummates the marriage with her].'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a man to finalize a triple divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorce by establishing that physical consummation is the prerequisite for the finality of the third divorce. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the literal requirement of 'mas' (touching/consummation) to reset the waiting period (iddah) and divorce count, ensuring the husband cannot bypass the three-divorce rule through mere verbal declaration.
